summary.text: An observatory is a location used for observing terrestrial, marine or celestial events.
Astronomical observatories are mainly divided by location into space-based, airborne, ground-based and underground-based.
Ideal sites for modern ground-based ones have dark skies, many clear nights, dry air and high elevation.

facts.label: Dome housing
facts.value: Most optical telescopes sit inside a dome or similar structure

facts.label: Best ground site
facts.value: Ridge A in Eastern Antarctica, per a 2009 study

facts.label: Mauna Kea Observatory
facts.value: Near the summit of a 4,205 m volcano in Hawaiʻi

facts.label: Highest observatory
facts.value: University of Tokyo Atacama Observatory, at 5,640 m

facts.label: Airborne examples
facts.value: The Kuiper Airborne Observatory and SOFIA use airplanes

items.prompt: An optical telescope sits inside a dome. How does it look at different parts of the night sky?

options.label: The telescope stays still and the sky is rotated
The dome's roof slit opens, and the upper dome rotates
The dome is removed completely for each target
The roof is sealed shut and a camera looks out

items.explain: The dome has a slit that opens during observing and closes afterwards, and in most cases the entire upper portion rotates.

items.prompt: A planner is choosing a site for a new optical observatory. Which site fits best?

options.label: A low valley beside a big city, shielded by hills
A humid coastal town with a busy harbor
A flat plain with frequent cloud
A dry, high mountain far from major cities

items.explain: Ideal sites have dark skies, a large share of clear nights, dry air and high elevation, away from population centers because of light pollution.

items.prompt: A new radio observatory is built in a valley, which would be a poor choice for an optical one. Why does the valley help?

options.label: It gives extra shielding from interference by radio, TV and radar
It makes the air thinner
It gives a clearer view of the sky
It lowers the effect of atmospheric turbulence

items.explain: Radio observatories keep away from electromagnetic interference, and unlike optical ones they can sit in valleys for further shielding.

items.prompt: Space telescopes avoid the effects of atmospheric turbulence. What is the trade-off?

options.label: They cannot see ultraviolet light
They are always smaller than ground telescopes
They cost much more to build and are very hard to maintain
They only work during the day

items.explain: Space telescopes are much more expensive to build than ground-based ones and extremely difficult to maintain.

items.prompt: A team needs infrared observations and expects to upgrade its instruments often. Why might an airplane observatory beat a satellite?

options.label: Airplanes fly higher than satellites
Airplanes fly above the whole sky
Airplanes are used by amateurs only
Upgrades and repairs are quicker and cheaper

items.explain: Airborne observatories rise above most of the atmosphere and, compared with space telescopes, can be deployed, repaired and updated much more quickly and inexpensively.

items.prompt: One ground telescope and one space telescope have a similar aperture. Which usually shows finer detail, and why?

options.label: The ground one, since it is easier to point
The space one, since its images escape atmospheric turbulence
Neither, since aperture alone sets the detail
The ground one, since it sees through more air

items.explain: Above the atmosphere, images are free from turbulence, so a space telescope such as Hubble often has a much smaller angular resolution than a ground one of similar aperture.
